_readme: Labelled retrieval pairs. `easy` are the original 25: near-quotes carrying the paper's own distinctive vocabulary, kept so the recorded baseline stays comparable. `hard` are paraphrased claims whose gold paper sits beside near-identical neighbours in this corpus — BERT against RoBERTa and ELMo, LayerNorm against BatchNorm, DPR against RAG — and which avoid the signature terms that made the easy set trivially separable. Recall@5 saturated at 100% on the easy set alone, so it could not tell two embedding models apart; that is what the hard set exists to fix.

queries.query: Replacing recurrence entirely with self-attention allows sequence models to be trained with far more parallelism.
Scaled dot-product attention computed over multiple heads lets a model attend to information from different representation subspaces at once.
Conditioning a language representation on both left and right context simultaneously during pre-training improves downstream sentence-level tasks.
Masking a fraction of input tokens and predicting them is an effective pre-training objective for bidirectional encoders.
Adding identity shortcut connections makes it practical to optimise networks that are hundreds of layers deep.
Framing the layers as learning a residual function relative to the input eases the degradation problem in very deep vision models.
Training a generator against a discriminator in a minimax game lets a model learn to synthesise realistic samples without an explicit likelihood.
Adapting the learning rate per parameter using running estimates of the first and second gradient moments works well for noisy objectives.
Stacking many small convolutional filters instead of fewer large ones improves large-scale image classification accuracy.
Sufficiently large autoregressive language models can perform new tasks from a handful of demonstrations in the prompt, without gradient updates.
Careful tuning of pre-training hyperparameters and training for longer on more data substantially improves an existing masked language model.
Splitting an image into fixed-size patches and feeding them to a standard transformer encoder is competitive with convolutional architectures at scale.
A smaller network can be trained to match the softened output distribution of a larger one, transferring much of its generalisation ability.
A siamese encoder fine-tuned with a similarity objective produces sentence vectors that can be compared with cosine distance efficiently.
Learned dense embeddings for questions and passages can outperform sparse term-matching retrieval for open-domain question answering.
Combining a parametric generator with a non-parametric document index lets a model ground its outputs in retrieved evidence.
A dimension-reduction technique grounded in manifold theory can preserve more global structure than t-SNE while scaling better.
Word vectors that vary with sentence context capture syntax and polysemy better than a single fixed vector per word type.
Shallow log-linear architectures can learn useful word vectors from very large corpora at a fraction of the training cost.
Vector arithmetic over learned word representations captures analogical relationships between words.
A first-order approximation of spectral convolutions lets neural networks classify nodes directly on graph-structured data.
Normalising across the features of a single training example rather than across the batch suits recurrent architectures better.
Normalising layer inputs using minibatch statistics permits much higher learning rates and reduces sensitivity to initialisation.
A new boson with a mass near 125 GeV was observed in proton-proton collisions, consistent with the predicted Standard Model scalar.
The diphoton and four-lepton decay channels together yielded a local significance above five standard deviations.
Conditioning on both the left and the right context at every layer, rather than concatenating two independently trained directional models.
Word vectors taken from the internal states of a deep bidirectional language model, so the same word gets a different vector in a different sentence.
The original pretraining recipe was undertrained, and removing the next-sentence objective while training longer on more data closes the gap without changing the architecture.
A model given only a task description and a handful of demonstrations in its prompt, with no gradient updates at all.
Producing sentence vectors that can be compared with cosine similarity, because comparing every pair through a cross-encoder is too slow for clustering.
Masking a fraction of the input tokens and predicting them, as a way of pretraining a bidirectional encoder.
Dynamic masking applied afresh each epoch rather than fixed once during preprocessing.
Scaling the parameter count by two orders of magnitude to see whether task-agnostic performance keeps improving.
Normalising over the features of a single training case, so the computation does not depend on the size of the mini-batch and works in a recurrent network.
Normalising each feature across the examples in a mini-batch to reduce the shift in layer input distributions during training.
A normalisation scheme that behaves identically at training and at test time, needing no running averages.
Higher learning rates become usable and the network is less sensitive to how its weights were initialised.
Depth was increased by stacking many small three-by-three filters rather than using larger receptive fields.
Layers are reformulated to fit a residual function relative to their input, which makes very deep networks easier to optimise.
Splitting a picture into fixed-size patches, embedding each one and feeding the sequence to a standard encoder with no convolutions.
Accuracy degraded as plain networks got deeper, and the cause was optimisation difficulty rather than overfitting.
A dense retriever trained on question-passage pairs outperforms a sparse term-matching baseline on open-domain question answering.
Combining a parametric generator with a non-parametric index that can be swapped out to update the model's knowledge without retraining.
Two encoders trained so that a question and its answer passage end up close together in the same vector space.
The retrieved documents are treated as a latent variable and marginalised over when generating each output.
Learning a single vector per word type from very large corpora, cheaply enough to train on billions of words.
Vector arithmetic on the learned representations captures syntactic and semantic regularities.
Per-parameter learning rates computed from running estimates of the first and second moments of the gradients.
Bias correction is needed because the moment estimates start at zero and are biased towards it early in training.
A small model is trained to match the soft output distribution of a large one, which carries more information than the hard labels.
Raising the temperature of the softmax to expose the relative probabilities the cumbersome model assigns to wrong answers.
Dispensing with recurrence and convolution entirely, so that path length between any two positions is constant.
Position must be injected explicitly because the architecture has no notion of order on its own.
Two networks trained against each other, one producing samples and one estimating whether a sample came from the data or the generator.
A minimax game whose solution has the generating distribution matching the data distribution everywhere.
Propagating information across graph edges with a layer-wise rule derived from a first-order approximation of spectral convolutions.
Classifying nodes when only a small fraction of them are labelled, using the graph structure itself as the supervision signal.
A dimension reduction technique grounded in Riemannian geometry and algebraic topology that preserves more global structure than its predecessor.
The excess is observed in the diphoton and four-lepton channels with a combined significance above five standard deviations.
The mass of the new boson is measured to be near 125 GeV, consistent with the Standard Model scalar.
Pretraining on unlabelled text and then fine-tuning the whole model on each downstream task, rather than freezing the representations.
Transfer from a large pretrained model to image classification, where the advantage only appears once the pretraining set is very large.
Reducing the cost of comparing many candidate passages by encoding them once, in advance, into a searchable index.
An architecture change that removes a bottleneck limiting how deep a network can usefully be trained.
Removing an auxiliary pretraining objective turned out to help rather than hurt downstream performance.
